fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**
Dressed stone blocks — large, flat, rectangular, laid in courses. But I have to be honest about how I know that: at the size shown I cannot tell. Under the lamp I can name it for one stretch of one edge. Everywhere else the answer is "a dark grey field," and if you put a hand on it you'd learn more than the picture told you.
fields.Q1_WHY: The only material evidence is the south face of the north wall, y230–264, between roughly x=250 and x=560. A vertical profile at x=330 reads: 4px black cap at y230–234; a course of blocks y235–246 warm-tinted (26,20,17); a 2px mortar line at y247 (13,10,8); a second identical course y249–262; another mortar line at y263; floor from y265. Two courses of ~14px blocks with mortar between them — that is masonry, drawn properly. It exists nowhere else in the frame.
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**
At the size shown: **a flat pattern around the edge.** The one place with a thickness cue is the north face just described. The west edge (x=55–56) and the south edge (y≈773) are a 2px seam and nothing more — no face, no cap, no top-vs-side value break. Magnified, the mass is real: the flat grey field north of y=237 is wall top, not another room, because the corridor floor at x385–435 carries hatched flagstone detail while the grey either side of it carries none. So it *is* solid, and the picture doesn't say so.
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**
Three different answers, which is the problem.

- **North (x=330):** 34 pixels of transition, y230→265, described above. This is good work.
- **West (y=430–530):** two pixels. Floor at x58–98 means (5.6,5.6,7.6)→(6.7,6.7,9.1). Outside at x0–43: (7.4,7.4,9.7)→(7.9,8.0,10.3). **The wall is brighter than the floor it encloses.** The transition is a 1-level step in the wrong direction.
- **South (x=300–420):** floor y760–772 = (10.4,9.0,9.4); outside y776–788 = (13.0,12.3,14.7). Same inversion, same 2px seam.
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**
**NOTHING.** No lintel over the corridor mouth at x375–440. No pin, rope, bracket, strut, shore or patch anywhere on any standing surface. There are exactly two objects on the walls in the entire frame: a small post-with-three-rungs sprite at x134–148, y190–228, and an undetailed dark vertical bar at x566–572, y190–228. Neither spans anything, neither meets anything, neither bears load. Cut both and the frame is unchanged.
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?**
**Repeated**, and I can prove it. The 64×38 block at (0,150)–(64,188) is **byte-for-byte identical** to (192,150)–(256,188). Across the whole north wall top, adjacent 64px tiles differ by RMS 1.3–3.5 out of 255 once you remove the brightness offset — max 4–6 levels. A 2432-pixel patch of that wall contains **12 distinct colours**. That is one tile stamped eleven times with a light gradient laid over it.
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?**
**YES.** It would ship.
Merely competent, or genuinely good? For the standing structure: **not even competent.** Three of the four room edges are invisible at played size and two of them invert. That is a functional failure, not a polish gap. The north wall's two-course face is genuinely good and is the only thing in the frame arguing otherwise.
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES AT 1:1?**
Legible at 1:1: one thing. A row of rectangular blocks along y235–265, from about x=250 to x=560. Outside that span the same band is black.

Blank at 1:1, plainly: the entire west wall (x0–56, y240–770) — I cropped it and looked, and it is an unbroken dark field with no readable edge against the room. The entire south wall below y=773. The wall tops north of y=230 across the full width.

Only on magnification: the coursing seams in the wall top at y≈186 and y≈232; the block subdivision of the top surface; the two props at x134–148 and x566–572. Nothing else appears at any magnification — no grain, no chipping, no mortar variation, no dirt, no repair. The surface has nothing on it to find.

Distance dependence: yes, and backwards. The north **face** is lit correctly — sampling y238–260 in 64px bins across x gives 5, 5, 6, 11, 18, 23, 14, 10, 6, 5. That tracks the lamp. The wall **tops** do not: y150–186 across x gives 12, 10, 11, 10, 10, 8, 17, 11, 12, 12 — dead flat, and the reading directly under the lamp (x=380) is 8, the *darkest* in the row. The west wall column at x40–54, walking down its whole length: 10.6, 10.7, 11.0, 11.2, 10.3, 11.3, **5.0**, 7.4, 8.0, 7.2 — the lamp is at y≈490, and 5.0 is that bin. The wall right beside the light is the darkest part of the wall.

**The wall tops and the west and south walls are not in the lighting system.** They render at a flat ~10/255 constant. Near the lamp the floor climbs to 124 and the wall reads as a dark hole, which looks fine. Six tiles out the floor drops to 5 and the wall's constant 10 overtakes it, and the room turns inside out.
fields.Q8:
ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**
Two things.

The **two pure-black rectangles** at (0,6)–(246,133) and (567,6)–(749,133), both RGB (1,1,2), both starting at exactly y=6 and ending at exactly y=133. They are the highest-contrast shapes in the picture and the only true black in it. Their edges are machine-straight and align to nothing — not to the corridor at x375–440, not to the 64px tile grid, not to any wall. Reading top to bottom, they are what the eye lands on first, and they are an absence with hard corners.

And the wall itself, which is where the eye stops trying. The repeat at (0,150)/(192,150) is exact; the near-repeats at 64, 128, 256 differ by 4–5 levels. Once you notice the wall top is one rectangle-field with a horizontal seam at y≈186, you see the same seam at the same height in every cell across all 750px.
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**
More of the same stuff. The flat grey above y=237 is the top of the wall mass, extending north at least 100px — I read that from the corridor at x385–440 carrying flagstone hatching while the grey flanking it carries none. So it isn't void, it isn't another room, and it isn't unnameable: it is wall, and it goes on.

What it is *not* is dark. The stated subject is "the darkness beyond," and beyond the walls sits at a flat 10–12/255 while the unlit floor inside the room sits at 5–8. Beyond the walls is brighter than the far end of the room. The two black rectangles at the top are the only real darkness in the frame and they are a reveal-system artifact, not a place.
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END?**
Found it — x375–440, running north from y=237, one tile wide. I read it as **a passage**, and the thing that made the difference was the block course: the face at y238–262 terminates cleanly at x=375 and resumes at x=440 with proper end-blocks. That is a doorway.

Tonally it gives you nothing. At the mouth, the gap reads 23 and the wall face beside it reads 18 and 14 — five levels. Further up, at y200–228, the gap reads 17 and the walls either side read 19 and 17: the way through is *darker* than the stone. At 1:1 it registers as a faint vertical bar of slightly-different-grey. It works because a draughtsman terminated the course correctly, in spite of the lighting rather than with it.
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**
No. Nothing has happened to it at all. It carries no damage, no settling, no spall, no accretion, no soot, no repair, no wear at the corners, no variation between one block and the next. The 2432-pixel sample at (0,150)–(64,188) holds 12 colours. This is a wall that was placed, not a wall that has stood in continuous heavy use since before records begin. For a fiction whose whole premise is four hundred years of unlovely competent patching, the walls are the one surface that has never been touched by anything.

---
fields.CULL: Wall tops are unlit flat fill — three of four room edges are invisible at played size, two inverted.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Put the wall tops and the west/south walls into the same lighting model as the floor, so the wall is always darker than the ground it bounds — at x40–54 the wall must not read 10 while the floor beside it reads 5.
- Extend the two-course face treatment at y230–264 to the west and south edges, so every boundary has a drawn thickness rather than a 2px seam.
- Break the wall-top tile: (0,150)–(64,188) is byte-identical to (192,150)–(256,188), and neighbours differ by ≤5/255. It needs per-tile block variation, not a gradient over one stamp.
- Put condition on the standing stone — spall, displaced blocks, soot, and at least one visible orc repair (driven pin, lashed timber, hide patch) spanning something, at a contrast that survives at 1:1.
- Raise the corridor mouth at x375–440 above its flanking walls in value, and drop a lintel or jamb detail on it, so a passage is legible without relying on the course termination alone.

Next thing I'd want to see: this frame re-rendered with the walls in the light model, before any texture work — that one change decides whether the other four are worth doing or whether the wall art was fine all along and the compositor was throwing it away.

*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*
